newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African regional strikes have mixed success.
newsitem.headline: S.African regional strikes have mixed success.

text.p: A second 24-hour strike, called by South Africa's trade union giant Cosatu to protest at new labour laws, had varied success on Tuesday in the two provinces affected.

The Durban Chamber of Commerce and Industry said the strike called by the Congress of South African Trade Unions in KwaZulu-Natal had been about 70 percent effective and cost business "millions". No exact figures were available.
"The strike had varied response from all economic sectors. Some reported an almost full turnout of workers and others were quite hard hit," chamber spokesman John Bryce told Reuters.
Toyota South Africa Ltd shut down its Durban-based manufacturing operations for the day losing production of up to 430 vehicles, a company spokesman said.
Portnet, which operates Durban port, Africa's busiest harbour, said breakbulk handling had been halted and container services were 67 percent operational.
Business and labour have deadlocked on core issues in the proposed Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
Labour wants a 40-hour working week and six months maternity leave, four of which would be paid. Business is insisting on a 45-hour week and four months maternity leave.
The new legislation is due to go to parliament next month.
Business chambers in Mpumalanga province said smaller firms were barely hit while collieries reported varying absenteeism.
